title: Void Ending in a Square to Jupiter
source: Picatrix (adapted), Book I chapter 4, Book I chapter 5, Book II chapter 3 and Book III chapter 1

<!-- generated by tools/content/gen-void.ts; edit the generator, not this file -->

The square is one of the two worst aspects in the lunar doctrine, an enmity the text grades as moderate because the signs it joins stand two natures apart. The counsel that guards every election runs exactly here: watch the square and the opposition in everything, and keep the Moon from the unfortunate planets in these figures above all.

When the Moon closes her course in a sign with a square to Jupiter, the quiet stretch that follows carries something of his temperate growth. Jupiter is the Great Fortune, hot and humid and temperate, the source of growing power: law, legality, jurisprudence, wisdom, the interpretation of dreams, and the ready winning of requests. His benevolence fits clergymen, kings, and lords; tin is his metal, the emerald and every shining white stone are his, and his animals are the beautiful and harmless ones once used for sacrifice. Set in the ascendant or at mid-heaven, the text says, he and Venus together rectify the Moon's misfortunes.
